items.title: Joe Robichaux Interview, 1959-03-19
items.q: And we had a guitar player called Kudu.

ctx.x: Roy Palmer, I'm not to say, Roy Palmer, not Eddie Palmer, Roy Palmer. So then I came back to New Orleans and I stayed about two months and I joined a show named Washbone and Weaver. And I went out with that show. And I played on shows, Tom Moss, went from Washbone and Weaver to Tom Moss. And I came back to New Orleans and I went out and played with a band they called the Black Eagle. That was E.T. Thomas, trumpet player from Crowley, Louisiana. Well, I played with him about two years. And I married, got married…
Now do you remember who else was in that band? Was Lawrence Dewey?

Lawrence Dewey was playing clarinet. We had a clarinet. We had Robert Gilbert. He was playing a C melody. Then he got an alto after, a little later. And we had a fellow that called Casey on bass. Walter Thomas was the drummer. That was E.Vance's drummer. And we had a guitar player called Kudu. I never did. That's the only name I knew him about was Kudu. He played guitar player. Nice guitar. So then finally...
